name: Technicolor
garments: not a fashion look — a film color process

media.title: The Wizard of Oz (1939)
media.note: the process's most iconic single use (the shift from sepia Kansas to color Oz)

reacts_against: nothing — it's a specific physical technology (three strips of black-and-white film, each exposed through a different color filter, recombined in printing) that happened to produce unusually saturated, stable color, later imitated digitally as a nostalgic look long after the real process stopped being used.

findings: dark — about 57% of the measured color across 4 Commons photos is below mid-lightness
mostly muted — about 87% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Wikimedia Commons images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
